content.title: Layout Starts With Flow
content.hook: HTML gives a page a sequence of content. Before you add special layout rules, the browser already knows how to place that content in its normal flow.
content.context:
Think of normal flow as the browser asking, “What comes next?” One piece takes its place, then the next piece follows it.

That default is useful. You do not need a special layout system just to put one paragraph after another.
goals: Understand that elements normally enter the page in document order and that layout starts with normal flow before extra layout rules are added.

content.title: The useful model
content.text:
Normal flow is not the absence of layout. It is the browser's starting layout behavior.

When the default result is already correct, leave it alone. A good engineer does not add machinery just to prove they know machinery.

content.prompt:
Create one heading followed by three paragraphs. Then add a fourth paragraph without changing any layout rule.

Observe the new content.

Your job is not to force a position. Your job is to notice what normal flow already gives you.
guidelines: State your reasoning clearly in your own words or code.
Compare your response with the reference guide after submitting.

content.question:
Imagine the heading is removed from the document.

What is the strongest prediction?

options.text: The paragraphs move into the space where the heading used to be, while remaining in their normal order.
The browser keeps an empty heading there.

feedback.correct: The flow is produced by the content that actually exists. Remove one item, and the following content can move into the space it used to occupy.
feedback.incorrect: The flow is produced by the content that actually exists. Remove one item, and the following content can move into the space it used to occupy.

content.question: Which statement is the strongest starting rule for layout?

options.text: Start by overriding the browser's default behavior everywhere.
Start with normal flow and add layout rules only when the design requires them.
Give every element a fixed width immediately.
Move every element manually until the page looks right.

feedback.correct: Normal flow is the baseline. Good layout work changes the baseline only when the relationship actually requires something different.
feedback.incorrect: Normal flow is the baseline. Good layout work changes the baseline only when the relationship actually requires something different.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Layout begins with content moving through normal flow.
**Senior habit:** Before changing layout, identify what the browser is already doing correctly.
**Mastery signal:** You can predict where added or removed content will move without adding a layout rule.
